s1.syndrome_frame: Hyperlipidemia with variable response to treatment and potential issues with laboratory measurements
salient_findings: Discrepancy between direct and calculated LDL-C measurements
History of adverse effects from statins
key_facts: Patient is a 47-year-old African American man
Medical history includes hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and gastroesophageal reflux disease
Patient has been tried on various statins
Patient experienced hip pain and elevated liver enzymes while on statins
Fasting lipid profile showed LDL-C of 232 mg/dL off lipid-lowering agents
Direct LDL-C was 113 mg/dL in June 2014
Direct LDL-C was 115 mg/dL in October 2015
Calculated LDL-C was 170 mg/dL in December 2015
Apolipoprotein B (Apo B) and Lipoprotein (a) [Lp(a)] were measured in 2016

shortlist.label: Familial hypercholesterolemia

shortlist.label: Lipoprotein(a) hyperlipoproteinemia

raw.rationale: The patient's significantly elevated LDL-C levels despite normal direct measurements, along with the measurement of Lipoprotein(a) in 2016, suggest the presence of Lipoprotein(a) hyperlipoproteinemia, which can cause elevated calculated LDL-C due to its effect on lipid profiles.

rejected.label: Familial hypercholesterolemia
rejected.why: While the patient has high LDL-C, the variability in direct and calculated LDL-C levels and the absence of specific physical examination findings or a clear family history make this less likely.

rejected.label: Familial combined hyperlipidemia
rejected.why: This condition typically involves a combination of elevated LDL-C and triglycerides, but the provided information focuses primarily on LDL-C levels without mentioning significant triglyceride elevation.

rejected.label: Polygenic hypercholesterolemia
rejected.why: Although the patient has elevated LDL-C, polygenic hypercholesterolemia would not typically explain the discrepancy between direct and calculated LDL-C levels as seen in this case.

rejected.label: Secondary hyperlipidemia due to hypothyroidism
rejected.why: There is no mention of hypothyroidism in the patient's medical history or laboratory findings, making this an unlikely cause of his hyperlipidemia.

gold: Elevated Lipoprotein(a) causing discordance between direct and calculated LDL cholesterol measurements
